title: Hillside Driveway
description: A single-lane gravel driveway from the county road, across Mill Creek, to a house site on the upper bench. The map is a synthetic example (5 foot contours, 1,200 x 1,200 feet). The topography was digitized from `example.png` with the planning tools (`trace` and `grid`), and the options were engineered with `route`.

options.name: West Climb
description: The least-cost corridor. It climbs west of Mill Creek on gentle side slopes, crosses the creek where the valley is shallow (3 foot culvert at 10+82), and contours around the east shoulder to approach the house site from the east. Cuts and fills are under 4 feet, cut and fill nearly balance (a small export), and there are no walls. Five turnouts serve the single lane. **Recommended.**

options.name: East Bench
description: A shorter route that crosses Mill Creek low (3 foot culvert at 6+93), where the valley is deeper, and then climbs the east bench. The crossing needs fills up to 16 feet deep and about 4,000 cubic yards of imported borrow, which outweighs the shorter length.

options.name: West Climb Paved
description: The West Climb alignment with asphalt paving instead of gravel - for comparison, the paving adds about 45% to the cost score. Consider it if the owner wants a paved driveway or the steep sections erode.
